pratku vgimel yakoz gest z czerwiku
ta chowati w puzdru gizto aby nevylil
ral potom kdyzby tedo byl ramen me
yaku branu tehdy vezma tu bran
rozhrzyzuy gi mahieno na vhli rzezane
y miezy tomu sadlo weprze divoko
a pomaz te brani tim sadlem a hnet
vnektere m miestie ramieny gest tau bra
ny nam se vypreysti kupige[s] k tu
nato miesto posypiz prachem swrchu
psanym obwazati tu bran a polozti
wpokogne miesto na poduzku na pryzlie
Ab hoze any wstudenie any gi zo
[illegible]rniowati wie nam kdugy, neb gy
[illegible]welmi skodij raneinu a tak
budes rano a wegek przewazowat
pomazie zadlem zasypat a wracy
ny tolko vgiste vodie [illegible]atobrna
[illegible] na ranu [illegible]la[illegible]i [illegible]ude
label: fol. 204r
translation: [illegible — the text contains difficult-to-decipher medieval Czech describing wound treatment with a salve made from certain ingredients, instructions for applying it to wounds, and directions for dressing and bandaging the affected area, with warnings about keeping it neither too warm nor too cold, as this could harm the healing process. The final lines mention dressing the wound again in the morning with the prepared ointment.]

text:
Item giny obyczey tehoz bo[ta]

Persicaria

[G]eni wondrzeye bozie alchymisti
kdyz kdo ranien aly rana byla twrda weza
mi tu bylinu gesto sluzy persygaliu
nebo dalsk a tez blesnik czinicz vrbi
ge ktoraz v potoku roste neb v rzicz
pomnij aly przwe rzicz na ranu vlozila
kladeno vogin tak wezma tu vrbigy
przilor zi na ranu a nechzi na rani
rozt se gohe nami zahrzeye z gi poffe
dij mista skrytelo lbe kamenij lozij a
wezma zty ranij tu vrbigy gi przwor
ten kamen a tu vrbigi ktoraz gt
lezicla kranie neb na ranie, wondey
tau skanau krmi a wezma ten kam
zas wurdiey na tu vrbigy: Ostry
tako gjak kmen lzicl aly geho tij
zafe na tu vrbigy vlozil, abude
se sama ranij hogiti przikladage
nami [omazkye] wzisty
label: fol. 204v
translation:
Item, another custom of this [herb].

Persicaria

[Whoever] by God's grace practices alchemy [medicine],
when someone is wounded or has a hard wound, let them take
this herb, which is used as persicaria,
or knotweed, and also the blessed one that makes wounds,
which grows by the stream or by the ditch.
Remember, first lay it upon the wound
when it is placed thereon, so take this little herb
and apply it to the wound, and let it remain on the wound;
it grows so that it brings forth [relief], and in [its] [power]
this place hides, it lies as a stone upon it, and
take from the wound this little herb and prepare it;
that stone and the little herb which is
lying on the wound or on the injury, place
that chewed food [poultice] and take that stone
again, place it on the little herb: likewise
as the stone lay, so too it [should be done]
again placed on the little herb, so
that the wound heals itself when this is applied,
and [it will] anoint [and] heal completely.

text:
wdie wyjdniwz ginym sudym zwon
zat, neb ta wrbicy fniki bude podtim
kamenem a rana se bude hogiti

Tyto trzi kusy sau skuffenj

Item wezmi kosti perwai a opalegi
na prach a tim paprlem zasyp rany
z kterijz blidnost teze

Item kdyby se komu przihodilo zutij
byl ramen z brogi ardomatau a
nebo strzellau tez poftzelen trzewnan
Ten naspiech wezmi kuen zazwey a
vloz wtepla na ranu a rozstrzel grue
wytahne a nemafti kuere norre mu
ziesnyziti svrke a rozpustiti teplau
wodau a przyloz na ranu tez pogrni

Item kuen stawiti odkudkoli

wezmi merz ktery nedost na vfkr
wacz vmelgich zidi a przyloz ter
ranu a chuid pogednau kuere stane
a takowych wiezzy do bgj thorrati
tedy se przygde swiet
label: fol. 205r
translation:
...in this manner goes out with other judgments...
for this little willow bark [root] will be under this
stone and the wound will heal.

These three remedies are tested:

Item: take bone [or: the first bone] and burn it
to powder, and with this powder sprinkle the wounds
from which paleness comes.

Item: if it should happen to someone that he be
wounded by a crossbow bolt or an arrow,
or shot and also wounded internally —
take at once the root of ginger and
place it warm on the wound, and it will draw out
the shattered piece. And anoint it anew, thoroughly,
to soften the skin, and dissolve it in warm
water and apply it to the wound, also warm.

Item: to stop bleeding, wherever it may come from —

take moss that is not lacking on old
walls, dry it, and apply it to
the wound, and quickly at once it will stop,
and such wounds will heal well,
so that one will see the light again.

text:
Komu zili sau przetiaty

od hembarta, w zihorzijm zjifa wjecz
Trito maff odielati ana ranu gij
nekiasti, nez przstu as od rany nedo
tikal zgedny zdrufe strany aby
zili zafe zerffwiek ofe zporzili
Zyto wierzy wezmi. kaprady czi
nacz pztzosowy pyro tozen attfe oflup
kadij tozen zinacz mu zdarms rzihnys
natznik, palichwy koien zzibny
ka oflupiti. zmiery hemeno grd
nofo datt gako druhefo szarym
fadlem ti wiezry fflucy podle rozi
Jinyfko, a tu wiecz fchowati do na
dobij att ne wiefra ato na fflaft
potom dat a vziwat bez potrzeba
Hazie A mañ Hazi na
rany zwobygzjnu kerzuzby pogiti
moffe
label: fol. 205v
translation:
For one whose veins are cut

[The remedy is prepared] from comfrey [hembart], in a green [fresh] state, thus:
A third part is to be prepared and applied to the wound
without pressing, but let the finger not touch the wound
on either side, so that the veins may again
properly come together and heal.
Take as much as you believe [needed]. Also fern
and plantain seed, likewise, let it be peeled;
then likewise differently, let it be given to drink,
bitter root [nettle root?], and the willow root peeled similarly.
Mix together with this another similarly prepared
tallow; with this smear it, following
the manner [instruction]; and this remedy keep stored
properly so that it does not spoil, and use it for healing.
Afterward give it and use it as needed,
according to the matter. And one may give this
to wounds in general use, as is customary
to apply.

text:
Klivost komu yde z klaubu holby

Temu klivost ge z klaubu a nemuz ho
z stawiti, tak vzin vezmi musskata-
vowy kuku na wohni yi wyziezij a
vsus na zieknu zieni, a vezmi zia-
bich stanazpek tez vsus yze to droze stluc
ay mosdirzi rownymi mieram yedno-
ho yako druzeho a tim prachem za-
sypey

Toto yest Trank wybor
ny k wssem ranam a zasstzela

Wezmi fanyel, Benedikt a yazyk
wolowy a hyinkastu na Appatece
a lystu swiatoweho a korzen rangi-
abozyho z zlutym kwietkem Grindatu
a wratycz Prusstizku obogi a to borze-
ny mass wariti v winie nebo wpiwie
Vcu tobu Pezy yest surte bozwrnij nebo
ty zeliny Pakli yest z zelenebo
borzeny nebo z zeliny tyz tuhyi stlu
label: fol. 206r
translation:
When one has joint pain from the joints

If the joint ache comes and cannot be settled, do thus: take muscatel nut, roast it on a fire, then dry it and grind it into a powder, and take ginger-root likewise, dry it, and grind both finely in a mortar in equal measure, one as much as the other, and sprinkle this powder [on the affliction].

This is an excellent remedy
for all wounds and sores

Take fennel, benedict root, and ox-tongue, and hyacinth from the apothecary, and St. John's leaf, and the root of orange color with yellow flower of celandine, and tansy, both kinds, and boil this root in wine or in beer. Use it [if] the matter is thick blood, or those herbs. But if it is from green root or from herb, then grind it likewise finely.

text:
ztluka ge vojtiseni zmich tu vodu nebo
tak zjich daruyz v mine neb v pivie darnie
zige dvakrat neb trzikrat za den, a
polozmu naranu zelezny zupen pisti-
miz tak dobze nez geli jako kapusto-
vy list ten vsehni dobze cziny

Item mast dobra kranam

Wezmi luy kozlovi a przistegyzige
mast rownymi mirami potom wezmi
drzewienny oley wlezz na rendlik przi-
zini medu cozt si zda slizto wszferko
wchwomadu wzpustie, pak wezmi kviet
kozy bradku zetgi geyi na prach a syp
do wndliku missuy riecl at se wzechn
dobze a budes gmiti masti

Mast kterzem zaranam a zlomani
ruky y nohy

Wezmi jarau manku a kmirznau a
zlarum zwoyrje mut drzewienny
oley a wosku natra tak riato tau
masti patraz a przikladey
label: fol. 206v
translation:
Grind it and soak it in a mixture of this water or
take the juice in wine or beer, drink
it twice or three times a day, and
apply to the wound an iron compress
so that it works as well as cabbage
leaves do — this remedy does everything well.

Also, a good ointment for wounds

Take goat tallow and prepare it
in equal measure, then take
pine oil, melt it in a pan, add
honey so that it becomes thick, mix
it all together and let it settle, then take
goat's beard flower, grind it into powder and sprinkle
it into the mixture, stir thoroughly so that everything
blends well, and you will have an ointment.

An ointment for wounds and broken
arms and legs

Take fresh butter and chamomile and
melt them together with pine
oil and wax, spread it onto
the ointment and apply it as a plaster.

text:
Proti dnawenu neb wogenstwu
masu od kosti

Wezmi kamenye ziweho nepaleneho za
peniz, sadla nersworzdneho a ztluc ka-
mence naprach, y sfunduy tim sadlem
a wwdey na wlizko, ale se ho rozpu-
sti missky nepatrzi, ast bude cjo mast
hotowa, sta hengila wzjmy sporzi-
bie a plastrzem stat na worzenstwi
maso a stazet byt bylo doff welky

Kdyby nohu neb ruku sobie wylomil

Wezmy kostiwal a stare sadlo stlucz
to wsochowadu a modre sukno wezmy
a wloz nato sukno te masti a obwiny
tim suknem, tu wywinrultinu

Proti weytcze nohy neb ruky

Wezmi zmieru pokruti wotrusstgemu
blinu spalenu y rozpitte to oslim
oczte, att gest jako kassse, y naklady
tusse na modre sukno a tim genu ob-
waz, at se trze gaby mohl gredny z
vgeti probalu
label: fol. 207r
translation:
Against gout or swelling of flesh from the bones

Take live, unburned limestone the size of a coin, [and] pure lard, and crush the limestone into powder, and mix it with the lard, and spread it on a cloth. But do not let it dissolve too much; when the ointment is ready, take it and apply it as a plaster onto the swollen flesh, and let it stay on until it has had its full effect.

If someone has broken their leg or arm

Take comfrey root and old lard, pound it together with vinegar, and take blue cloth, and put the ointment on this cloth, and wrap it around [the limb]; this will help it heal.

Against swelling of the leg or hand

Take a measure of crushed bran, burnt henbane, and mix it with donkey's vinegar until it becomes like a paste, and spread it on blue cloth, and wrap the limb with it, so that it may draw out [the swelling] and the person may walk again properly.

text:
Proti primu:

Vezmi kamenec bili v rodě trpli
neztal a tim vsta vymyvati zwyka
te nielo vuoge a potom luzyti voget
vymyvati vezmvz hus kastru roz
hiezti a hvie zdravi:

Item ktomuz jarna golbi

Vezmi kamenej palenyho a muska
torvau kulku a przeslizku samal
przeslizku vezma vtoru sucztu voun
Dej namj tu przissugiczi przislizku a
spal gi na prazk v swndrij tytrzi
tviegi vchromedu a sluz at gi
prazk, y vezmi drabet medu voun
Dej ty wiezy vo chromedu a sluz at gi
Da toho medu vmichej a woundej na
gazyk tyi nazegtrj druhym vtora
A potom czervenym skarlatem nebosu
czem gazyk tyi nazegtrj druheho
anem
label: fol. 207v
translation:
Against the first [ailment]:

Take white alum, [prepared] in a bitter
manner, and with it wash the mouth, accustomed
to this remedy, and afterward have it
rinsed; take a piece and grind it fine
and let it heal.

Likewise, for this, a spring remedy:

Take burned stone and musk,
a ball, and crushed resin, [or a] similar
crushed resin, take another dose therein.
Give to us this adhering crushed resin and
burn it into powder; and insert it twice
into the wound, and let the mucus be
powdered. And take a bit of honey therein,
give these things into the wound, and let the mucus be
[treated]. Mix this honey and insert it onto
the tongue; let it stand a second [time],
and then with red scarlet cloth, without
wrapping, let the tongue rest a second [time]
and so on.

text:
O Nemogych w hrdle
tomu zasijczek spadne zinak zipie

Wezmi medu a popel turzeneho wezmu
gey do medu spausstigy trzy do hrdla
A zas neyde ~

Na hrdle otok zenzslowe zinba

Zlista a skussena ovien od zhotskeho
Wezmi hti ktere roste przimorzimarti
zato przi sprontem gyarw wazy namen
Skrzisti vzliky a hndagi przimien
Lozyez kozen yeho wazy trzy zistie w
bilim pivie a day nemocznemu piti
aby pozhzti moh a att vzymiyrowat vsta
sobie a roztrczu se boleti massnyky

Jtem ktere ditie ma podgeti

Vzin takto wezmi lozy srabky kwiet
zni gest brunatny vsuf trzy a rosle
mezy pseniczy a setzi probet kuk
ky massflatuoy wdzeley stoho prach
obogiho a przides klomu probet
medu sawey ditiki
label: fol. 208r
translation:
On those who are sick in the throat,
when the little uvula falls, or otherwise one gasps for breath

Take honey and ash from burnt [something], mix
it into honey, drip it three times into the throat,
and it will not return.

On swelling of the throat, the swollen gums [or tonsils]

A proven and tested remedy from the physician:
Take the root that grows near the sea-rosemary [rosemary],
taken beforehand with the grain, weigh out a portion,
crush it well and knead it together.
Take its bark, weigh three parts, steep it
in white beer and give it to the sick person to drink,
so he may swallow, and let him rinse his mouth
with it, and the sore flesh will dissolve.

Also, what a child should be given

Do it thus: take the scrapings, the blossom
that is brownish, dry it, and grind it
with wheat, and sift it, prepare it well,
mix it with fat, in the evening, make from it a powder
of both, and bring it to him; prepare it
with honey and give it to the child.

text:
Zienam Lekarztwij

Przistupowanij Matky y zprdczij
wezmi Cybzel yzop pelynek a
wazz v wodie ne stawie a wezm stk-
str ztoho pod samy pupek

Aby Matka wostupila na swe miesto

wezm podkaurzenij zespodku skrze na-
czwku wezmi Glawiczky chmelowych
kadidla wonotku yalowcze a ztoho
wdielay podkaurzenij zi.

Zista a prawa wiecz od mladi

komy z Bilowreho na mnozeyssi wie-
czerz skussena kteraby zierna die-
tiatka nemohla miti nebo se to trefuge
Bie mnoha snim vmrze zi. y na
Kowadech gst kosstowano na skrawach
Norwazich Swinich listuch, czi-
by zim toho dano nebylo sporodem
musijlby Zemzyti
label: fol. 208v
translation:
Medicine for Women

Approach to the womb and the heart:
take onion, hyssop, wormwood, and
boil in water that is not standing, and take a strip
of cloth from that, [and apply it] right under the navel.

So that the womb returns to its proper place:

take a fumigation from below through a
tube; take heads of hops,
incense, juniper berries, and from that
make the fumigation [prepared as above].

A certain and true remedy from youth

[tested/proven] from Bílovice, for the most part
tried, so that a child's seed
could not be had, for it happens
that many die with it. And it
has been tested on anvils, on the skins
of Norwegian swine's hides, so that
if it were not given to them, by nature
they would have to perish.

text:
Vezmi vody čisty zdyvlik a hrnec
nowý poliwaný a do toho hrnce wli
tu wodu A patom wezmi czibule czerwe
ný a gi oblup pak ty lupiny czo se
zda wrazdeg da ty wody gz czwarz
tu spolu wšeho vbli az to gisctiew
uge a tak ty wody polowicze wezmi
y szczedisz to pieknie a gisteho hrnyzka
lupiny za hrsti tu wodu zlupin
tiezl przistan krwosni a wrazdeg do
te wody Gazla gisteho kusstu czi
ztu az se dobrze rozpline wby wo
dig Gezys zdemie se toho napiti te
kolku honadrum vbli toho po hizgi

Aby nikdy ne ozab

Kdyz se ditie narodi zmatuge Chnud
Trnu zmaz sadlim hushym nozgy
a ruze nehšteprzim pak ze tep ro zmeg
a nebudesz gizby niekdy
label: fol. 209r
translation:
Take clean water, a jug
and a new pot, and into this pot pour
that water. Then take red onions
and peel them, and afterwards their peels, as you
see fit, destroy them. Take that water a fourth part
together, as much as will be enough,
and take half of that water,
and you will clear it nicely, and in the first pot
place the peels by the handful. That water from the peels
let it stand, let it clot, and then destroy it in
that water, and crush of the first kind
until it dissolves well with the water.
Then let one give to drink this
a small amount, hold it in the bosom after this is done.

So that it never freezes [i.e., so it never gets frostbitten]

When a child is born confused, take an insect
of the thorn, smear with thin lard the nails,
and the rose on the fingertips, then warm it well,
and it will never be sore.

text:
Ditieti proti osutinie

Lékařstvie najlepšie Ditieti která
býše vřelo osuti, nejprvé aby vtepl
chováno bylo a vlažiti potom vezmi
jeho semena a čistie ze žebřice a vžen
dat do čistého hrnečka poléváného
a to vumdal lušky nali nato vína
bieleho a vlažiti dat píti Ditieti a
vysyp se namie

O nakaženém žaludku

Pan Barkory z Gromnicz proti
nakaženému žaludku kterýž osut ne-
má, [bedlu] zas napraviti gry
vezmi šalvěj zermielu persán
celanku čebřiček jednoho klako
suchého vař vezysti vodie v obie
a při tom bez budeš mieti jíti ležat
a rano a opolednie Cesta 24 47

Ite knížišším person: yzop salvěj
tolu v starém pivie vařiti neb víno
a vduli bypiek lyne rano a vegzrtepk
label: fol. 209v
translation:
For a child against rash/eruption

The best remedy for a child who has a burning rash: first, keep the child warm, then take its seeds and clean dill, and put it into a clean, glazed little pot. Let it [steep/soften] and then add white wine, warm it, and give it to the child to drink, and the rash will go away.

On a corrupted stomach

Mister Barkory of Gromnice [gives a remedy] against a corrupted stomach which has no rash, [and] to restore appetite for food, take sage, germander, parsnip, celandine, thyme, one [dry herb], boil it, take water from both, and with this, without [further ado], you shall go lie down, both morning and at noon. [Recipe reference] 24, 47.

Item, for distinguished persons: hyssop, sage, boil in old beer or wine, and [administer/drink] in the morning and evening.

text:
Jíž proti smrádku a nebo kdož jest
neduživ w žiwotu

Wezmi zazwor. Zawřij popel czyzým
zalgan hověz prustworcy toho rozwo
wzýti czdnostojný znýzie to masý to
mohti za ni dni a potom pa ni
znerk piz to a wtom sobě omazéj
tapenisku a stim kozrmim jez a pi
rana a weczer

Proti Czerwene Nemoczy

Prawa wecz od pana Kyliana hofmi
stra Welowskeho Wezmi kozrim
Natužniku gest kayen Czerwený
kwitek nest zluty ze wsiffe kozen czistie
sluey gey czistie cw mazerigi a coz
wazij zlatij toho prazku dey muzi
cw napogi bud ani wimi neb w
bijlim pirwie partli gest mladenecz
coz wazi toho prazku za pul zlatyo
tomu dey wypiti patli dihe za cztwrt
zlatw muze fati Czrusona wiez na
mnozyog
label: fol. 210r
translation:
Here against foul stench or whoever is
afflicted in the belly/body

Take ginger. Cover with ash, cut up
boiled beef broth, of that the same amount
to use properly, cut it up so that
it can last for several days, and after several
days make a mixture and in it smear yourself,
heat it and with that same mixture eat it, in
the morning and evening

Against the Red Disease (dysentery/bloody flux)

A true recipe from master Kylian, court-
master of Welowsko. Take root of
knotweed, it is called the Red
flower, not yellow, cleaned well of all skin,
grind it clean, make a powder, and as much
as weighs a zlatý [gold coin weight] of this powder give to a man
to drink, whether to a woman or to
a child, first it must be a youth
as much as this powder weighs for half a zlatý
give him to drink; a girl, long enough for a quarter
of a zlatý can take. Crushed [this], it is known to help
many.

text:
Strzewo kdyż wychazy

Wezmi kus prena boroweho a roz-
krzyzy ge sadrze a wezmi wina neb
oleij raspi domieseij kamenicze, girol
mozi wlom kus sutkna ath gest to
teple prostrzy nato prawu a necht
walom sedij

Tez Wez prach wdieky z dobre
mysli a tim prachem Strzewo zasep
pak a Diwoznowy list nato przylo-
ziti, to spomaha.

Bista Wiecz proti ka-
menu od pani Barbory z Chromie

Wezmi Gemeno posledowny asy roznij
zen a to rozetrzeti a wnapogi pati
aby czlowiek wsseho zapotil se

Binag

Wezmi kwiet Brzezowy trnowy
a Glohowy wdielat prach ztoho
a Darwat wnapogi knieze tho-
masse Bilowskeho
label: fol. 210v
translation:
The tree/shrub, when it comes forth

Take a piece of pine wood and
split it with resin, and take wine or
oil, sprinkle and mix in a stone-forming
substance; grind a piece of cloth so that it
is warm, spread it there properly, and let
it sit for a while.

Also: Take powder gladly with a good
mind, and with that powder sprinkle the
Tree remedy, then apply mullein leaf
to it; that helps.

Here follows a remedy against the
stone, from Lady Barbora of Chromice

Take mixed [herbs], various kinds,
grind them and give in a drink
so that the person sweats thoroughly.

Another remedy

Take flowers of birch, blackthorn,
and hawthorn; make a powder from this
and give it in a drink to Father Thomas
Bilovský.

text:
Koho vsseckli pes vkaussne

Bud glowieka neb howado napiss
tato slowa na chlebu kyry czerniclem
tri krsti glowieka neb howadu
+ karva + kataliez + Alelffint
anferna + Chrelkin + od oz-
waldu kalisse koffmistra wilowske
tento kus gest wydan

Proti Rarowy kosti

Nim tato Boleft tuto rarowu koft
Jako gest minula boleft pana na-
sseho Jezisse krista kdys trbyl trazen
Y mluwyl wstali geymeno otze
Y syna Y Jucha swateho
At wen mass rzikati toto zaklinani
po tri pattky rano
label: fol. 211r
translation:
Whoever a dog bites, mad with rabies

Whether it be a man or beast, write
these words on bread with a quill
Cross a man or beast three times
with: + karva + kataliez + Alelffint
anferna + Chrelkin + from Oz-
wald the chalice-bearer, master of wiles
This remedy is issued

Against the Night-Demon's Bone

Take away this pain, this demonic bone
Just as the suffering has passed from our Lord
Jesus Christ, when he was tormented,
And spoke, having risen, in the name of the Father
And of the Son and of the Holy Spirit
One should recite this incantation
Three times each morning

text:
Swateho Walentina nemoc

toho napadne paducý nemoc neb slowe
swateho walentina nemoc, ten odielen
sobie pas z kuzie wlczi [...] gest my
pasli zierna z kuzie wlczieho a gesti
ziwota swyniu wundat, a kdyz kdo
widiel an toho napadla. ten pasnu
niem mia zrzazati gelo a to kopati
kdyz asi czlowieka zhlaubiy, a ten wlczy
ma na sobie nossiti, ale ma ten byti ke
rezy ty nemozy mitey newidiel.

Proti paliczy

Kdyz kun pige, tehda rozumu gest z aust
tuze to wezma y mystim ty potrzebu

Na dimicze

Wezmi tiesta od premtany z ktereho
peczin peczau a tim tiesten kladssli
naty potrzebu prany die gest wiro:
zitezna:-
label: fol. 211v
translation:
The Sickness of Saint Valentine

This illness strikes as the falling sickness, or it is called
Saint Valentine's sickness. One should prepare for himself
a belt from wolf hide [...] it is made
from grain and from wolf hide, and from the
belly of a pig that has been wounded, and when someone
has seen that it has struck [the sufferer]. One should then at that moment
take from it [the hide] and dig it out
when it is as deep as a man's [reach], and this wolf('s hide)
one should wear upon oneself, but this must be done
so that the sickness is neither felt nor seen.

Against Epilepsy

When a horse drinks, then reason comes forth from its mouth;
take that strongly and apply it as needed.

For Fevers/Chills

Take dough from [a certain preparation], from which
bake a cake, and with this dough apply
it as needed; wash it, as it is said to be
effective.

text:
Proti bolení zubuov

Vezmi tet trawu yz trnowa do zahrady
kdyz chceš k stogi proti slunczy rownyma
nohama trzyky tyz Otcze nass trzy Zdra-
Maria gedno wezmy w ruku to zrzie-
kage potom tuto modlitbu

Mila zemie zaluogi tobie bolezni
mnie zuby proszym tebe odeymi tu bolest
odemne tak kusto, az budu zas vtobie
wezmenu Otcze y Syna y Ducha svat[ého]
tuto modlitbu potrziekaty rzieky

Potom natom miesti tez stanes rownyma
nohama tu trawu wub.. tyn den podgez
tyz tak rzyky yaku nazyj rzsi potom
ten den obrat zas nato misto trawau
doluow y odtud prwjz, a potom
sielaty mietle w samie zdi nabo mieste
z czesti kdyz chyde nechoz

Kazena na mnohych
label: fol. 212r
translation:
Against toothache

Take this herb from the thorn-bush into the garden
when you wish to stand facing the sun with feet
together, say three times Our Father, three Hail
Marys, then take one into your hand and look at
it, then [say] this prayer:

Dear earth, I complain to you of pain,
my teeth, I beg you, take away this pain
from me, so help me, that I will again be in you
taken, In the name of the Father, Son, and Holy
Spirit, say this prayer and give thanks.

Then stand again in the same place with feet
together, [take] this herb ... that day pull it
again, saying the same words as before, then
that day turn again to that place, the herb
downward, and from there pull [it] out, and then
scatter [it] into the same soil or place
from whence it came, do not withhold it.

Tested on many.

ley prach zmich geyz mas steptim ogle

v wag ge samy a kdyz budau te
ple zmaz ten kun tim neb psa
tuchegz toho tak at samo odpadne
opiet wzin tez o tak kazdeho z hogise

lidomie a wezma gey Dobre sluz a

paustiey gi vde krtize sau zlowieka
label: fol. 212v
translation:
On how blood clots/curdles

Take [the herb] Zternowek (sloe/blackthorn) and law[fully... prepare]
ley powder from it, which you shall at the right time
give to drink of this powder, and from
it the blood shall thereby dissolve and
go out smoothly, as is fitting

Which horse is mangy or [which] dog

And this is the pure remedy, only white
for this, take krasnicz (knapweed?) with white [something]
in weight by itself, and when they shall be
full, smear that onto the horse or the dog
with it so that it may fall off by itself
again use the same for every such healing

Another remedy for ✤ scrofula (king's evil)

Take [the herb] "Between the Hands of God"
[Gelidomie/pellitory?] and take it, a good service it does, and
soak it in wine, dip it into the wound and
apply it to scrofula on a man's body

label: fol. 213r
translation:
Also, here is another remedy against scrofula (goiter):

Go into the field for healing herbs, and a small head [of garlic/herb], take it for the throat. Then take the bones and wound(s) into a vessel properly prepared, and take with it the bones with this wound into a hot oven, and when the bones are well dried, grind them or pound them into powder, and with this powder sprinkle the scrofula sores and they will heal.

A remedy (tisane) from Mr. Labonský:

Take a handful of cumin seed with dill, this strained well, prepared properly, done thus for it. Take a portion, sliced finely, and prepare it in due measure — it is not necessary to [do more] — always when this remedy is prepared, sugar should also be added to it.

text:
Kohoz welmi hlawa buolí

Wezmi Cernobyl a Cemenec ozymí
a jalowec warz to spolu w wime
tak diuho dokuz se semenec nerozpuka
a kyz to vwrze wezmi seme
nec a jalowec zetri w bilim mazle
S oczim vsuse toperig a omoz to
penku wtom wlozi na time a pri
krej hlawu sobie dobrze:

Item posilnemi hlawy Wezmi
Yarau Mauku wlasky worzech Bili
mak Mandli kwet mufskatowy
hrzebiczky orzech muskatowy zazwor
bili zauati kmin anijz koliandr
Rzowy kwiet zetrí wsse spolu a roz
pust to wsse bilim winem zwarito
y bude kaffse y deyz genutu rano
a wezer tak mnogo gako wlaskj
orzech probatu?
label: fol. 213v
translation:
For one whose head hurts greatly

Take wormwood and winter cumin
and juniper, boil this together in wine
so long until the seed cracks open,
and when it boils, take the seed
and juniper, grind them in white ointment.
With vinegar, dry it in the sun, and wash it with that;
put a small portion of it on the temple and tie
the head well for yourself.

Also, to strengthen the head: Take
spring poppy, walnut, white
poppy, almonds, nutmeg flower,
cloves, nutmeg, ginger,
white cumin seed, anise, coriander,
rose flower; grind all together and dis-
solve all this in white wine, boil it,
and it will become a paste; give it in the morning
and evening, as much as a walnut's
worth, tested.

text:

ode spat

Wezmi czelidon y škulu oczy s starym
winem a medu prziczinie ktomu a
pepřz bielého trzinieho a maz oczy
cžistie bielmo seydie

Wezmi salweyi yzop pokoj kukwiczi

A vmoczez teple
label: fol. 214r
translation:
Item: whoever has heat in the nostrils
And also pain in all the limbs

Take fat and separate from it what is proper to it
and apply it to the nose, to the forehead, but gently,
so lightly. Take also a kernel from walnut shells,
prepared from its own nuts, the shell only,
equal in weight, and pound it
well in a mortar, then mix it
with egg white and spread it on paper
and apply it to the forehead, but keep it warm
toward sleep.

Against pain and film on the eyes

Take celandine and wash the eyes with old
wine, and add honey to it, and
white pepper finely ground, and anoint the eyes;
the white film will clear away.

Against cough and hoarseness

Take sage, hyssop, peony, cowslip,
white and red wormwood of the finest kind, together
with burnet, basil, and marjoram;
boil this down and let it settle, then drink it warm,
and moisten it while warm.

label: fol. 214v
translation:
[margin note, unclear]

Ezipa (a plant/herb) is hot and moist and has many
powers. Whoever cooks it and consumes it entirely
destroys the goodness in the body and clears
obstructions. Likewise, whoever uses it rightly
heals everything that is harmed
or injured in a person, and
dry coughs it soothes; also whoever eats it
with olive oil or another
preparation gains unspoiled flesh and
becomes more supple in [illegible].

Kalkan has these powers: when a
person releases blood, kalkan applied to the wound
drives out bad blood and brings
forth good blood; it has another power too: whoever
applies it washes away all stench of decay
in the gums and mouth and relieves shortness of breath, and dusty throat;
whoever takes it with wine eases thirst and relieves
strong poisoning, and it is a good remedy — truly
effective when held beneath the tongue.

label: fol. 215r
translation:
All of it is of value and dear;
the fifth is that whoever mixes it with wine and Jewish
wine anoints with it: that day the head will not
ache. The sixth is that whoever washes and changes [it]
as happens with great sorrow, when one
causes men to vomit and under the tongue
holds it, it will soon be to his health;
applied. The seventh is that if anyone

The eighth is that this woman on all her

[red:] On digestion
Remedy [herb name]

Cook it with apple and drink well, consume it;
if it is proven, also with May ointment
and with honey, whatever in a man is broken
or dislocated, all of this it will heal
and return to its place, and in a new moon.

label: fol. 215v
translation:
Thus says Master Avicenna: Whoever
has seen one struck heavily on the brain,
let him roll about until he becomes exhausted
in his struggles, and then quickly
lay him on his back, and from this
he shall be healed.

On the brain and the head

The rose is a flower of very noble
virtue. Whoever washes himself with its water
around the brain and around the crown of the head
heals also inflammation and pain of the eyes,
and also strengthens the growth around the brain.

The violet also has such power for the brain. Whoever
chews it and places it on a wound, it
removes all pain. Likewise, whoever applies its juice
to the head draws out all harmful matter
and does not allow wild flesh [proud flesh]
to grow. Thus whoever uses its seed
or its juice, and washes the head of a sick person
with it, relieves pain quietly
and draws it out.

ktere pivo mumj strati

Sprawa wyborne wlozenij

kadtbla, przetworze Benedictu rzeb

stawagj.
label: fol. 216r
translation:
Which beer/mum goes bad

Benedikt — there are two kinds, white and red.
If one wishes to drink red Benedikt, when
his own wine/must has spoiled, then one
may soak it in red wine, and
when it is soaked, add it to the vessel and let it steep
for a day and a night. Likewise, whoever mixes it
will find that the other also becomes red
and of good color. Likewise, in whatever
house or chamber it is kept, there will be no
harm, nor grief, nor anything unworthy
that can remain there. Likewise, whoever drinks it mixed,
let him not fear, nor be troubled.

Instructions for excellent preparation:
First take fresh calamus. Plantain,
cuttlebone, prepare Benedikt's... 
boil it in a vessel and put it
into the barrel, and the beer there shall altogether
be improved.

label: fol. 216v
translation:
Sage has these powers:
whoever eats it for two or three days,
boiled with salt, everything salty and sensed,
it serves one with its power,
it soothes and steadies. Also, whoever grinds it
with good wine and applies it to the stomach,
all sicknesses will be healed thereby,
and strengthened by its power. Also,
whoever grinds it, boiled with salt, will have no
swellings occur in the person,
but everything will be renewed and restored to health.

Holy Spirit root is
helpful against spells; whoever carries it
upon themselves and chews it against poison,
to consume it in drink, or in great
power drives out poisoning. Also whoever
boils it in water and drinks it all,
will drive away rawness and sickness of the heart,
or hot fever — it also helps with this.

translation:
Whoever would place it on a wound and bind it,
or whoever would be bitten by a mad dog—

Pale. Master Albalianus says that
when one lets water be poured inwardly,
it already heals excessive weakness
and also the disease of the spleen, and
softens hardness, and wondrously
removes water, dissolves obstructions in the blood,
and thus stops bleeding from the book (veins?).
When this distilled water is mixed
with rose-water and birch-water, and
one anoints oneself with it, it quickly cures
all sickness in him completely.

label: fol. 221v
translation:
Against miscarriage of the fetus

[Advice] of Master Jan Starc of Swolesslaws[?]
Take beet water and give it to the person
to drink for three days, in the morning,
at noon, and at night, and for those three days let
him eat little and rest, and let him be alone without
much talking to people, and let him stay in a cool place, and
let him avoid all rich food.

Furthermore, so that this may be done for
the person, take from the apothecary water
of knotgrass, a small measure of violet water,

a third part of rose water, a small measure
of citron water, and mix these together,
and for those three days wrap this
around the head while warming it, always three times
a day, after each drink of rose water.

Also, this is done so that the fingers
stay clean and fresh, and the feet so that one does not suffer
numbness: wash them three times a day with
warm vinegar frequently, and after that let one put
between the toes a pinch of salt under the nail, on two fingers.

Wine, that... boil the root and waters,

Against sleeplessness and against raving (madness/delirium)

An eternal remedy, I recommend to everyone
beforehand... take both, cook it, (boiling)
likewise the root with... Ambrose, more
or less, a certain amount. Mix it together, O good one, and
combine it together to weigh it fittingly, that it be
thick, so that with this warm (mixture) the head
may be treated.

translation:
Whoever bleeds and whose bleeding returns—
[illegible] from the stomach, and will not give him comfort...
This man had blood coming from him;
he stopped the blood with wine or with standing, a drink,
he had him drink it from the bottle, out of it the blood...
There is no need to seek anything else [illegible] says the chamberlain.

For a wound that has gone bad and rotten in the flesh:
Take dried parsley leaves, grind them into powder,
and sprinkle it on the rotten spots and it will heal them.
Or without that, smear on the wound black ointment
made in water — that, says the honorable chamberlain,
is the very best for this purpose, believe it.

Against rheumatism:
Take [illegible], put a little frankincense into it,

Take the little bell-flower that creeps along the ground — some call it
"vizel" — boil it in wine or
beer and give it to her to drink, so as not to lose it; this too
the chamberlain [illegible] confirms as another precious remedy;
let one give it to her often.

Against burns, very good and certain.

Take salt and [illegible] a little

So that one has no freckles on the face.

Take sap of white oak and of dodder (bindweed),
white and clean, and take Italian wine

smear it on the face in the evening and
let it stay there for a few minutes, then this

So that a woman does not miscarry her child.

Take alder [bark/leaves], while still green,
dried, prepare a decoction, strain it,
mix it with wine or with goat['s milk], anoint
with it, [give to] the mother to drink in small
sips.

Against internal colic pains and gripes of the stomach.

Take three or four pieces of true
balsam, give it to drink mixed with wine,
three times warm, and it will pass quickly.

translation:
For correcting the stomach

Boil an old hen in water until
the bones become soft, then strain the liquid,
you wish to [add] good myrtle, hyssop,
sage, ginger, add a little knotgrass (?) and
salt lightly, use as food.

A purge for the stomach

Take vinegar which is boiled with [substances] equal
in proportion, strain it in a basin, let it
drip well through, then take
cow's milk, strain it well, fry it,
place it in strong vinegar, mix it again,
take a little of this, warm it while straining,
apply this cloth to the sick person's
navel, and let it adhere, and when it has begun
to work, he will soon have a purge.

An example of a plaster called "apo-
stolicon"

Take burnt copper, ground to powder,
burnt, white lead well purified,
half a pound of wax, one ounce of [something],
melt all of this together in a pot and
put it on a good fire, then
strain it, and stir it well as it boils.

Tento plast skazie mus tewati tak slauho
az se rana zawrze zgaby welku hodu
label: fol. 225r
translation: Into cold water in a mortar [put]: galbanum, sarapinum, ammoniacum, opoponax, colophony, mastic, frankincense, litharge, myrrh, sarcocolla, bdellium, quercitron, Armenian stone (lapis armenus), gum arabic, terebinth. Take of each about one lot (a small weight measure), crush these ingredients together, then pour them into cabbage-water that has been drawn from these herbs. Set this over a gentle flame and stir with a spatula constantly so that it does not stick or scorch. When everything has dissolved, take it down from the fire and add to this ointment a wax that has melted, together with its fine powder, not too coarse. Then the water will thicken; stir it again until it dissolves. Afterward pour it into cold water, then take it out of the water and knead it between your hands while it is still warm; smear it on the skin, turning it over so that it is well mixed and set aside. This plaster, once made, must be kept warm for a long time until the wound closes, so as to give great relief.
